approachGroups._note: Round 21. Named sets of outside nodes that say where a through car comes from or is going, in words a resident uses. Gates are placed by the first rule that matches (street names and classes at the gate, whether trips can only enter or only leave, and the compass bearing in degrees clockwise from north from the study area's center to the gate). Other outside nodes take the group of the nearest surface gate (ASSUMPTION). `overrides` (node id to group id) fix gates the rules place wrongly. `sets` are named unions. The reserved id `study-area` stands for the nodes inside the study area.

throughIntents._note: Cut-through reasons. Hypotheses about why a car crosses the study area without an end in it, in words a resident uses. A through trip that uses a residential or service street of the study area is tallied under the first reason that fits, in this order: the SR-24 on-ramp it will use (ramps are derived from the network, tools/lib/ramps.ts; the car's planned route at the moment it is counted), the off-ramp it came by (the links it has driven), or, for a trip that uses no ramp, the first reason whose fromGroups holds its origin group and whose toGroups holds its destination group; any other goes under Other. Groups and sets are those of approachGroups. basis `observed`: a volunteer or agency count of a turning movement, a freeway share or a ramp limits how many cars the model sends this way; where they come from and why is still the model's assumption. basis `assumed`: no count limits it. `avoids` is the arterial the trip would otherwise use on the shortest free-flow route with the side streets closed (an assumption of the calibrate report, not a driver survey). A ramp reason is listed for each ramp that carries about 3% or more of the PM peak's through cars; the rest go under Other on-ramps and Other off-ramps.

judgedZone.source: ASSUMPTION (calibration round 37): cars cleared from gridlock count against the stability rule when held in the study area, on its bounding streets, at the junctions on them, or at a node within this distance of them along the network. A bounding street's queue holds a car beyond it by filling the cross-street link into its junction, so the zone must reach the first junction beyond each bounding street: 113 m away at the median, 200 m at the 75th percentile, 301 m at most. A queue that spills farther is a chain of held vehicles, which the rule follows to any distance

calibration.note: Not calibrated: PM held-out count stations pass 11 of 24 (rule: over 85%), and Colby St NB through cars stay above the counted range.
calibration.caveat: Round 42, PM peak. Since round 39 the trip estimate is fitted to the resident volunteer count of through cars on Hillegass Ave and Colby St (February 25, 2025), so those four figures no longer test the model; the checks that stay independent are the count locations held out of the fit, the share of side-street cars going to or coming from the freeway, stability and travel times on Telegraph Ave. Since round 42 the trip estimate also uses the simulator's own routes on 16 counted blocks of the street grid between Telegraph Ave and Claremont Ave, where the simulated drivers cut through far more than counted (Forest St eastbound into Claremont Ave carried 190 cars an hour against 66 counted, now 121). Over twenty seeds, Hillegass Ave southbound carries 116 through cars an hour (counted range 79 to 120; seed-to-seed uncertainty of the mean about 3), Colby St southbound 118 (39 to 117), Colby St northbound 150 (102 to 145) and Hillegass Ave northbound 92 (48 to 95). On Colby St northbound the extra cars join from Forest St, where the model sends about 77 an hour against 57 counted. All four freeway shares are within 10 points of the observed ones. The signal at Claremont Ave, Colby St and Forest St gives Colby St the 4 seconds of green the volunteers observed; the green for Forest St is not observed, and the model gives it about 37 seconds of the 79-second cycle, which draws cars through the grid. Since round 37 the limit of 1 car an hour cleared from gridlock applies near the study area (its streets, the bounding streets and 200 m beyond). There the PM peak clears none over two sets of ten seeds. Farther out it clears 1.2 and 2.1 an hour, mostly on Russell St and the hillside streets near Ashby Ave in Berkeley, a kilometer or more away, where the model has few counts; treat those streets as a weak spot at the edge of the model. The AM peak clears 0.3 an hour, all of it far out, and midday none. Resident-provided field observations, relayed by the project lead, show left-turn arrows for both directions of Claremont Ave at Ashby Ave, so each runs in a signal phase of its own; the timing is an assumption until a current timing sheet is found. Claremont Ave northbound carries about 370 to 410 cars an hour against 577 counted in 2010. The 2010 signal plan from a published traffic study (each Claremont Ave direction in its own phase) was tested and cleared more cars from gridlock, so it is not used. Residents also report two eastbound lanes on Ashby Ave at Claremont Ave; the model keeps the one lane of the map data, because with two lanes its signal timing gave Ashby Ave less green and cleared more cars from gridlock. Simulated drivers turning left on a plain green take gaps in oncoming traffic faster than a published capacity method allows when oncoming traffic is heavy; a stricter rule was tested and made the network less stable, so it is not used yet. Feeding the simulated delays back into the demand still did not give a usable demand: its iterations cleared 10 to 25 cars an hour from gridlock, nearly all far from the study area at Ashby Ave / Claremont Ave and on the hillside streets behind it, and left more trips waiting to enter the network than the current demand. Southbound Telegraph Ave carries about 1,280 to 1,290 cars an hour at Alcatraz Ave against 1,064 counted, while Alcatraz Ave from the west carries about 295 against 547, and Alcatraz Ave leaving eastward about 490 against 689: simulated drivers bound for SR-24 avoid delays on Alcatraz Ave west of Telegraph Ave and on Ashby Ave toward Tunnel Rd that the demand estimate does not see. Giving the demand estimate half of those delays cut the excess by half but cleared 15 to 17 cars an hour from gridlock far from the study area, so it is not used. About 140 trips an hour are still waiting at the end of a PM hour to enter from SR-24 at the west edge of the model, held by the one-lane end of the off-ramp to Martin Luther King Jr Way. Round 36 traced that gridlock: Claremont Ave northbound backs up from the one-lane stretch north of Ashby Ave, which ends at Russell St in an all-way stop. A resident confirmed in the field that every approach there stops, so the network is right; a count at Claremont Ave and Russell St would still show how much traffic that stop must pass. The left-turn pocket size, the lane-change settings and the distance for joint signal timing are assumptions. Lane counts on Stanford Ave, 51st St and Telegraph Ave just north of 55th St were corrected from map tags and still need a field check. The recent PM count stations pass GEH 5 at 84 of 92 fitted (91%) and 11 of 24 held out of the fit (46%); AM 70 of 77 (91%) and 15 of 19 (79%). Six of the PM held-out failures are state counts on San Pablo Ave, Ashby Ave and Tunnel Rd at the model's edge, each the only count on its entry, so a fit without it cannot place that traffic. Almost all recent stations come from one hour of one day of resident volunteer counting (February 25, 2025). Midday has no counts and is checked for stability only. Treat through-car figures, and changes between scenarios, as model output: on Colby St northbound it is still above the count it was fitted to.

Field observation by a resident, relayed by the project lead (2026-11-15): the northbound Claremont Ave approach at Ashby Ave has a left-turn arrow, so its left turn onto Ashby Ave is protected (DATA for the phasing). The 2010 PM Synchro worksheet of [SafewayCollege-DEIR2011] runs the two Claremont Ave approaches as split phases (northbound 17.0 s, southbound 17.5 s of a 100 s cycle) and codes the northbound approach as two lanes with no left-turn lane, which fits. ASSUMPTION pending a timing sheet: the approach runs in a phase of its own in every period (protected-only, not protected-permissive), and the cycle and greens follow the flows like any other modeled signal; the other approaches' phasing, the pocket length and the timing are not observed

Field observation by a resident, relayed by the project lead (2026-11-16): the southbound Claremont Ave approach at Ashby Ave also has a green left arrow (DATA for the phasing). With the northbound arrow (2026-11-15) and the 2010 PM Synchro worksheet of [SafewayCollege-DEIR2011] (both Claremont Ave approaches as split phases, Ashby Ave eastbound and westbound in one phase with permitted lefts), each Claremont Ave approach runs alone on its green. ASSUMPTION pending a timing sheet: every period, and the cycle and greens follow the flows (Webster) on that phase structure rather than the 2010 greens
